notes.title: Final Release
notes.notes: [p]Final Version Release[/p][p]Releasing the final version (Features/Gameplay) today. Based on the wishlist numbers and general hype What Lurks Inside did not quite reach the audience I hoped for. As a result, I won't be building on the current systems nor will I be changing the price. The price reflects the amount of content it currently has which while less than I wanted, still fully complete. Given the price is low and it is multiplayer, those who do choose to purchase will have enough content (with friends) to have fun. [/p][p]What Lurks Inside is and has always been multiplayer-focused so you will have the most fun with friends, you can play solo but the experience will not be very replayable. [/p][p]While I will consider this game feature complete, I will still be working on any bugs found and I will polish/ tweak the environment but nothing major. [/p][p]As always I appreciate everyone who supported me during early access, apologize for the smaller scale, and look forward to people enjoying the experience I created. [/p][p]Thanks all. [/p]

notes.title: Progress Update 2
notes.notes:
[b]<Note these changes will come in a Major update, this is just what will be in soon>[/b]

The new player controller is complete, works much better, and offers many more systems and minor features. Along with this significant change, the crafting system has been overhauled and split up per location. Each area will have some version of a crafting machine tailored to the area. The medical area for example will have a dedicated crafting machine for antidotes and other medical products. 

To address some balance issues with Uninfected vs Infected I have created several new systems that make playing as each fun but not one-sided. The main gameplay loop was updated slightly to, you will no longer need to just escape, instead, you must destroy all infected areas via a new system that allows you to create an airborne antivirus which needs to be created and administered via air system. This will push players to explore and engage with the main AI creature which functions similarly to Nemesis from Resident Evil games.

There are a ton more new features and systems, but I will go over those when the next game update is ready. I have not worked out if I will do the update in pieces or just once all systems are locked in. Either way, the price of the game will increase per update to reflect the amount of content currently available. Over the scale is not huge so the price will remain low in general.

Thanks again for all the support.

notes.title: Progress Update 1
notes.notes:
While I continue to develop the game, add new systems, and polish existing ones I wanted to keep the status transparent. These smaller progress updates are just that. Game design can be time-consuming, and I don't want it to seem like nothing is being completed. With that said here is a quick update. 

Progress is moving along well, however I did find a massive bug with the new player controller. Nearly all the in-game systems I created myself, except the player controller. Player controllers are quite complicated to get right, especially first-person multiplayer ones. The issue I was experiencing was considerable network lag, so much so it became unplayable. I spent a good month trying to fix it, and I did manage to locate the issue, however it is deep in the code. I was able to place a bandaid on it, but I was unable to fully fix it.   

While the fix helps I am not happy with the results. So I decided to take some time to learn all the ins and outs of making a player controller and create my own. I'm happy to say I was able to create my own and it's quite good. It's not complete and will take a bit longer, but it's a must before I can continue with the last few systems. 

This new player controller will be a game changer and allow for many things I was limited on while using a premade one. Better control and a great foundation to add new features. I'm looking forward to getting it ready and in-game for everyone to play.

Thanks again for all the support.

notes.title: Crafting (Coming in the next update)
notes.notes:
The upcoming update will introduce several new systems, remove outdated ones, and enhance others. While we polish and test these changes, I’d like to start sharing details about what’s coming. As the title suggests, the first spotlight is on Crafting.

I set out to create a crafting system that seamlessly integrates with the game’s environment and enhances gameplay with unique, lore-friendly elements. This system aligns with the game’s narrative and complements other mechanics. Players will need to craft essential items like power supplies, fuses, medicine, and more. As development progresses, additional blueprints will be introduced, expanding the range of craftable items.

How does the system work?
Each blueprint requires three distinct resources to craft. These resources can be found scattered throughout the map—on shelves, on the floor, and in other locations. Every resource is physics-based, meaning you’ll need to physically pick them up and carry them to the crafting machine. Once there, you drop the resources into the machine’s intake hopper, where they are added to its inventory. After gathering all the required materials, simply press the crafting button, and the crafted item will be dispensed from the machine’s output hopper.

What can you create?
Currently, you can craft Power Supplies, Power Fuses, one type of Medicine, and an Incinerator Tank. As the game evolves, additional items will be added, such as cures for new illnesses and components for other systems.

What is the end goal of this system?
The crafting system is central to mission completion, but it also supports and enhances other gameplay systems. For instance, if your character is knocked out repeatedly, you might develop vision issues that require a special crafted item to cure. This interplay is designed to make the system both functional and immersive.

What is the current state of the system?
The system is fully functional and highly flexible, allowing new blueprints to be added with ease. While the core mechanics are complete and unlikely to change during further development, updates and bug fixes will continue to refine the experience.

notes.title: Early Access Release
notes.notes:
Today, "What Lurks Inside" was released into Early Access. It may show as fully released (an error on my part), but I'm working on fixing that. The early launch also comes with a 15% discount for early customers. This current build of the game will receive a massive update that improves all systems, adds new systems, and removes/combines other systems.

I chose to release What Lurks Inside now with the last version so that anyone who wants to provide feedback and have a larger say in the direction of the game can do so before the game's foundation is solidified. 

PLEASE NOTE: What Lurks Inside is still in early access and will contain bugs and varying levels of polish. It will undergo many visual changes and minor gameplay loop changes. If you are looking for a complete game at this time, please refrain until more updates have been completed. I am looking at no more than 6 months to a year to reach full release in its current state. 

For those who support me, I appreciate you and will not let you down. Please utilize the forums or if you prefer join the discord. Your feedback is most valuable and I look forward to delivering a great experience to those willing to support the project. 

Take Care.
